submitted.rationale: Index 29 (Mg0.19Sb0.81) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0867%, ahead of index 26 (0.068%) and index 10 (about 0%). EQE rises toward the Sb-rich end. This fits MEGNet's narrower predicted band gaps there, below the 3.2 eV photon energy: MgSb2O6 2.8 eV, MgSb4O8 2.6 eV.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE was about 0. This Mg-rich region is dominated by wide-gap phases such as Mg4Sb2O9 (4.2 eV).

consultations.verdict: Support: MgSb2O6 (trirutile, Mg 0.333) is on hull per MACE and MEGNet HSE gap 2.8 eV < 3.2 eV photon energy, so it can absorb; Mg4Sb2O9 (4.2 eV) cannot. Measure near Mg 0.27-0.33.

Weak support: Mg3SbO4 (Mg 0.75) has MEGNet HSE gap 3.07 eV, just below the 3.2 eV photons, so it may absorb. Sb-rich index 26 gave only 0.068%, so I am testing the Mg-rich side for contrast. Mg3Sb2O7's 0.24 eV gap looks unphysical, so I am ignoring it.

Support: MgSb4O8 (Mg 0.2) has MEGNet HSE gap 2.64 eV, narrower than MgSb2O6, so it should absorb more of the 3.2 eV light. The measurements also point this way: the Sb-rich sample (index 26) beat the Mg-rich one (index 10). So I am measuring the most Sb-rich sample, index 29 (Mg 0.19).
